study type: Secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial
exposure: Socioeconomic status (high vs. low income, high vs. low education)
Women with high levels of fear of childbirth (Wijma-Delivery Expectancy/Experience Questionnaire ≥66)
outcome: Healthcare use (general practitioner and midwife visits)
Access to continuity models of care
cohort: 1410 pregnant women screened for fear of childbirth, with 339 reporting high levels of fear. Of these, 183 returned data on birth method and health service use at 6 weeks postpartum.
finding: While healthcare use was similar across socioeconomic groups, women with higher education levels had greater odds of receiving continuity of midwifery care.
mod_finding: Women with higher levels of education had greater odds of seeing the same midwife throughout their pregnancy, which is known to reduce the likelihood of cesarean section.
